issue_context.title: JSON schema validation returns wrong missing field on nested objects
comments: Transfer to `fast-json-stringify`
Yes, I can reproduce it with Fastify, and I can't reproduce it with fast-json-stringify standalone. But it looks like a fjs error. Finding the problem.
Should we transfer it back to Fastify?
yes
From the explanation above, the current behavior looks correct to me.

> From the explanation above, the current behavior looks correct to me.

What do you mean by `the current behavior looks correct`. It shouldn't serialize Fastify/FJS errors with a route serializer, right? It's still a problem.

Something wrong happens here:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/7cbad5819738183226184950259934de8ea90a2b/lib/error-handler.js#L99

> What do you mean by the current behavior looks correct. It shouldn't serialize Fastify/FJS errors with a route serializer, right? 

No, it should serialize the error with the given schema. It doesn't matter if the error originated from `FJS` or any other places.
When you specify a schema for a status code, it should follow that schema.

I strongly disagree with this statement. When I, as a user define response schema I can't (and I don't want to) predict all fastify errors that can be thrown, but I still want to see this error in my response.

When a user define a response schema for that particular route. 
That means he want that route to return in the contract, providing an error format that is never expected by the user is also unacceptable.

If the user want an unify shared schema for response or something that follow your will. 
The user should provide a custom error handler.

I don't understand your point. Let's take an example from this issue.

Now I'm on a client-side receiving an error:
`{"statusCode":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"\"ok\" is required!"}`
it has status code 500 and it doesn't match a user schema and that it's ok (IMHO)

I tell you I want to receive an error with a correct message:
`{"statusCode":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"\"token\" is required!"}`

How does it a different response format?

> I don't understand your point. Let's take an example from this issue.

When you use with `schema` and cop with other client.
Let's say mobile, they only handle the error with specified schema (see it when using `@fastify/swagger`).
Then, it returns the `fastify` error that is unknown to them.
Boom... the application doesn't know what to do (iOS most of the time will crash with unexpected `struct`). 
Not saying it can be so many other form error.
But Fastify returns an error that doesn’t match the schema.
I can take it. I'll create a PR for this.

> It doesn't match, but fastify returns it. I don't tell you that we should return different error structures. I'm saying that it should be a Fastify default 500 error but with a correct message.

It is also a correct message from the error itself.
You can never determine which error should be skipped and use the fallback.
You only know that we have a contract to follow and when the **final response** is not follow the contract that is.

You are saying we should skip in the middle and when is it?
If I specify an error handler that intercept the `fastify` error which schema should be used then?
We should return an error message if it was thrown by FJS and don't try to serialize it.
Not sure. I'll check later today.

@climba03003 After second thought, I think you're right. We should treat serialization errors as user errors. What I think we should do is include the origin error message [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/b8ae90a419775a922cb10bc889599aaae415e8bc/lib/error-handler.js#L118).

review_comments:
I would treat this change as "sensible" because some users may not expect the additional error detail

I'm +1 to ship it anyway
